blogs.title: When HIT Hits Early: Decoding Preoperative Heparin Exposure
blogs.description: Most clinicians are trained to look for Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) in the standard POD 5–10 window. However, this case highlights a critical 'temporal trap' where preoperative procedures—like cardiac catheterization—can prime the immune system. We will discuss why it's vital to audit the entire perioperative timeline, including sub-therapeutic heparin doses given days before surgery, when faced with early postoperative platelet drops.

blogs.title: Beyond the Standard ELISA: Navigating the Nuances of Autoimmune HIT (aHIT)
blogs.description: When the laboratory results are 'indeterminate,' how do you proceed? This post explores the fascinating world of autoimmune HIT (aHIT), specifically focusing on heparin-independent platelet activation. We'll analyze the serotonin-release assay (SRA) profiles that defy conventional classification and how to maintain a high index of suspicion for aHIT when clinical severity outweighs laboratory clarity.

blogs.title: Managing the Hypercoagulability Storm: Argatroban vs. Fondaparinux in Severe HIT
blogs.description: In severe HIT, standard anticoagulation isn't always enough. This post analyzes the clinical decision-making process behind switching from an IV direct thrombin inhibitor (argatroban) to fondaparinux. We will discuss the 'red flags' of consumptive coagulopathy—such as falling fibrinogen, rising d-dimers, and the appearance of schistocytes—and how they dictate pharmacological pivots in the ICU.

blogs.title: Stroke in the Setting of HIT: The High-Stakes Balancing Act
blogs.description: The risk of thrombosis is the hallmark of HIT, but a cerebral infarct in a patient with profound thrombocytopenia creates a complex management dilemma. We will discuss the tension between aggressive anticoagulation to treat hypercoagulability and the risk of hemorrhagic complications, specifically focusing on how to manage aHIT-associated neurological events safely.

blogs.title: The 'Indeterminate' Profile: When Antibodies Defy the Textbook
blogs.description: This clinical pearl focuses on the specific serological phenotype of aHIT where Fc receptor blockade is only partially effective. We will explore what this means for the pathophysiology of autoimmune responses and why clinicians must be prepared for 'atypical' lab profiles that indicate a more aggressive, heparin-independent disease state.
